estimates.narrative: Starting from a baseline near-term risk anchored at about 12%, the evidence nudges the probability upward due to CS detections and intelligence claims, but strong norms and practical constraints pull it back. The resulting calibrated estimate places the chance of any state actor using chemical weapons in Ukraine before May 1, 2026 at roughly 16% with a ±6 percentage point uncertainty.
summary: Anchor from near-term state-actor chemical weapons risk in Ukraine around 12%.
Documented battlefield presence of riot-control agents (CS/chloropicrin) and credible intel alleging Russian involvement push the posterior up.
OPCW monitoring and the normative prohibition reduce risk, constraining the posterior.
Delivery challenges and attribution uncertainties keep the probability non-negligible but not large, consistent with a 16% posterior for the 2025-2026 horizon.

justification.synthesis_rationale: Base rate anchor combined with modest upweight from battlefield detections and credible assertions, offset by norms, deterrence, and logistics; the horizon constraint (≤May 1 2026) further reduces the posterior, yielding a calibrated 16% with a wide but plausible uncertainty band. Calibration notes: 2-sided range is intentionally conservative given evidence quality and attribution ambiguity.

summary: Anchor at 12% based on reference class of state-actor chemical weapons use in modern warfare and the near-term horizon; May 2026 window extends beyond a single-year forecast, requiring calibration.
Up updates from battlefield detections of CS/chloropicrin and credible intelligence push the risk higher, signaling non-zero probability of escalation.
Down updates from OPCW monitoring, global norms, historical rarity, and horizon considerations pull the probability back toward a low-but-non-negligible level.
Net synthesis yields a central forecast around 10%, with an uncertainty range roughly 6–14%.

question: Will any state actor use chemical weapons in Ukraine before May 1, 2026?
summary: Ensemble aggregate for near-term risk is 14%.
Objections emphasize attribution uncertainty for CS detections and strong normative constraints, which push risk downward.
Horizon extension to May 1, 2026 introduces some upside if tensions persist, offsetting part of the downshift.
Threshold analysis supports a non-negligible but low near-term risk; anchor around 10–12%, with a plausible 10–15% range.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid and point to attribution uncertainty and deterrence effects that justify moving the estimate downward from the ensemble, though not to zero.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted downward from 0.14 to 0.12 to reflect strong downward pressures from attribution concerns and deterrence, while acknowledging a non-negligible risk that warrants a 10–15% plausible range.

forecasts.reference-class: Post-1945 modern warfare: baseline probability that a state actor uses chemical weapons in a contemporary conflict over a near-term horizon; historically rare with only a handful of confirmed uses (e.g., Iraq–Iran 1980s; Syria 2010s; and Ukraine-related incidents since 2022).

causal-factors.name: Battlefield detections of chemical agents (CS/chloropicrin) in Ukraine
causal-factors.rationale: Recent OPCW and partner reports confirm presence of riot-control agents on the frontlines, indicating ongoing capability and risk of escalation.

causal-factors.name: Credible intelligence and official statements alleging Russian involvement
causal-factors.rationale: Public assertions from the U.S. State Department and European intelligence about chemical weapons use raise near-term risk, though attribution remains contested.

causal-factors.name: OPCW monitoring and ongoing investigations under the Chemical Weapons Convention
causal-factors.rationale: Active monitoring and potential investigations strengthen deterrence and normative constraints, reducing likelihood of new uses.

causal-factors.name: Global norm against chemical weapons and normative consequences of breach
causal-factors.rationale: Universal prohibition and expected international backlash deter state actors from using chemical weapons.

causal-factors.name: Historical rarity of state-on-state chemical weapons use in modern warfare
causal-factors.rationale: Past conflicts show chemical weapons use is rare, anchoring the near-term probability at a low base rate despite isolated incidents.

causal-factors.name: Documented battlefield presence of riot-control chemical agents (CS) in Ukraine
causal-factors.rationale: OPCW confirmed CS presence in three October 2024 frontline incidents and a February 2025 report affirmed CS in battlefield samples with maintained chain of custody, signaling direct use of chemical agents on the battlefield (https://www.opcw.org/media-centre/news/2025/02/opcw-issues-report-second-technical-assistance-visit-ukraine-following; https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2025-04/news/opcw-finds-more-chemical-weapons-use-ukraine).

causal-factors.name: Public/intelligence claims of Russia using chloropicrin and riot-control agents
causal-factors.rationale: U.S. State Department and allied reports asserted Russia used chloropicrin against Ukrainian forces in 2024 and that riot-control agents were employed in warfare, elevating perceived near-term risk (https://www.cnbc.com/2024/05/02/us-accuses-russia-of-using-chemical-weapons-in-ukraine-in-breach-of-ban.html; https://apnews.com/article/26a1bea82a7d1a57b581c60683628712).

causal-factors.name: Strong normative framework and OPCW monitoring under the Chemical Weapons Convention
causal-factors.rationale: The CWC prohibits chemical weapons and OPCW monitoring, along with UNODA emphasis on limited uses since WWII, create a robust normative barrier that lowers near-term risk (https://www.opcw.org/media-centre/news/2025/02/opcw-issues-report-second-technical-assistance-visit-ukraine-following; https://www.unoda.org/en/our-work/weapons-mass-destruction/chemical-weapons; https://turn6view0.draft).

causal-factors.name: Delivery feasibility and strategic deterrence concerns reducing near-term likelihood
causal-factors.rationale: Analyses highlight significant delivery challenges and high political costs of chemical warfare, with some forecasters predicting near-term use is unlikely, despite long-run concerns (https://www.atlanticcouncil.org/blogs/ukrainealert/will-putin-use-chemical-weapons-in-ukraine/; https://www.atlanticcouncil.org/in-depth-research-reports/report/how-the-us-and-europe-can-deter-and-respond-to-russias-chemical-biological-and-nuclear-threats/; https://www.rusi.org/explore-our-research/publications/commentary/chemical-weapons-use-ukraine-tests-global-norms-breaking-point).

causal-factors.name: Time horizon constraint: anchor is for next 12 months; May 1, 2026 window is shorter
causal-factors.rationale: Swift Centre forecasts cite a 12% risk for chemical/biological weapon use in the next 12 months, which implies a lower probability when restricting the horizon to May 1, 2026 (https://www.swiftcentre.org/publicforecasts/russian-invasion-of-ukraine-outlook).

causal-factors.name: Attribution remains unsettled, reducing decisiveness of risk signalling
causal-factors.rationale: Even with CS detections, attribution to Russia remains contested, which dampens the certainty and urgency of escalation signals (OPCW findings; RUSI commentary) (https://www.opcw.org/media-centre/news/2025/02/opcw-issues-report-second-technical-assistance-visit-ukraine-following; https://www.rusi.org/explore-our-research/publications/commentary/chemical-weapons-use-ukraine-tests-global-norms-breaking-point).

causal-factors.name: OPCW-confirmed presence of CS riot-control agent in battlefield samples (Oct 2024 incidents)
causal-factors.rationale: OPCW technical assistance visits confirmed CS and related compounds on trenches and dugouts, indicating battlefield chemical agent exposure.

causal-factors.name: Credible intelligence alleging Russia's use of chloropicrin/CS in Ukraine
causal-factors.rationale: Dutch and German intelligence publicly claimed repeated use of banned chemical agents, signaling state-actor involvement and raising near-term risk.

causal-factors.name: Continued chemical weapons prohibition and OPCW monitoring
causal-factors.rationale: Ongoing enforcement of the Chemical Weapons Convention and active monitoring deter escalation and constrain use.

causal-factors.name: Delivery/logistical challenges of chemical weapons in Ukrainian warfare
causal-factors.rationale: Analyses note practical hurdles to large-scale deployment, reducing likelihood of a major chemical attack in the near term.

causal-factors.name: Attribution uncertainty and contested evidence
causal-factors.rationale: While CS findings exist, attributing responsibility remains contested, dampening certainty about state-actor use.

synthesis: CS detections indicate battlefield chemical presence but attribution to a state actor remains contested. Normative constraints and OPCW monitoring reduce near-term risk, while the longer horizon allows for potential upsides if tensions endure. A calibrated probability around 12% with a 10–15% plausible range balances these factors.
